newsitem.title: USA: Wisconsin unemployment remains at 3.4 pct in May.
newsitem.headline: Wisconsin unemployment remains at 3.4 pct in May.

text.p: Wisconsin's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate remained at 3.4 percent in May, the same as April, the workforce development department reported Monday.
The unemployment rate likely would have dropped lower if not for cooler-than-expected weather for the month, the department reported. The seasonally adjusted rate from May 1996 was 3.6 percent.

The department also said there is some statistical evidence to support the possibility that Wisconsin employers have been prompted to coax more workers into taking second jobs in the face of the state's tight labor market.
Employment statistics for the month show that 10,900 more people were working in May than in April, but employers reported having 52,100 more jobs available than a year ago, the department reported.

Madison illustrates the state's tight labor market, the department reported. The city's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate remained unchanged at 1.6 percent in May, the third lowest reported in the nation.

Job growth has been stronger than the national average in several major sectors for 12 consecutive months including construction, finance and real estate, manufacturing, government and services, the department reported.
